_comment: SSOT for Claude hook installation. Read by lib/sync/core.sh (which files to
symlink into $CONFIG_DIR/hooks) and by lib/common.sh:ensure_rules_enforcement_hooks
(which entries to reconcile into settings.json).
Before this file existed the two lists were maintained separately, so a hook
could be installed as a file and never wired into settings.json — it then sat
in the hooks dir as silent dead code. Adding a hook now means adding one entry
here; anything not listed is neither linked nor registered.
Fields: event = Claude Code hook event; matcher = tool-name regex or null for
events that take no matcher; script = basename inside runtimes/claude/hooks/.
Order is the order entries are appended to a fresh settings.json.
'run' is optional: a command template where {path} expands to the installed
hook path. Omit it and the command is `node "{path}"`, which is what every JS
hook wants. It exists because a bash hook, an env prefix, or a subcommand
argument cannot be expressed by the node default — the compact-gate entries
need all three. Note the matcher for PreCompact/PostCompact is matched against
the compaction `trigger`, and for SessionEnd against `reason`, not a tool name.
'retired' lists hooks this repo used to ship. Ownership is decided by asking
whether the repo has the file, so a hook deleted outright stops looking like
ours and its settings.json entry would linger forever. Naming it here keeps it
prunable. Entries can be dropped once every machine has synced past them.

hooks.enforces: injects rules-core.md as additionalContext every turn
rules-core rule 7 — incremental edit size (warn >300L/30KiB, deny >800L/80KiB)
rules-core rule 7 — closes the heredoc/tee/echo bypass of pre-edit-gate

a definition lookup typed as rg/grep is denied and pointed at serena. Measured cause: symbol tools are installed and prescribed in prose, and sit at 0-0.9% of 220 sessions while the one hook-backed channel sits at 44%. Narrow on purpose — quoted definition patterns only, serena-activated projects only; escape via ' 텍스트검색:'
rules-core rule 6 — token efficiency; staged by on-disk size, bounded reads pass
70-analysis 'oma-lab fail check first' — records failed commands and surfaces a repeat, without the model having to volunteer
hooks.requires: a Claude Code that sends PostToolUseFailure; present in 2.1.217+, verified against the schema shipped in 2.1.220

hooks.enforces: rules-core rule 6 — blocks a turn that edited a file without running a verification command
rules-core rule 3 — blocks a long multi-edit turn that never used the ToDo tools

10-context 압축 게이트 — defers auto-compaction to a work-unit boundary; exit 2 blocks, every failure path allows. One entry, not one per trigger: the manifest contract is one registration per script, and the script itself allows immediately when trigger is manual

appends one behavioural row per session to ~/.claude/uptake/rows.jsonl. The full ~/.claude/projects scan costs 30-60s and so only ran when someone remembered it — the same failure mode every measurement here keeps finding. Incremental (0.3s/session), and carries the two counters that answer whether symbol-search-gate works: nav.serena against its 0.9% baseline, and gate.escape as the false-positive alarm
clears a busy marker the session forgot to release; no matcher, so it covers exit/clear/logout/prompt_input_exit
